decisions.reason: The source says team reconciliation fell from five to two hours weekly, identifies the parser as the person’s contribution, and says coworkers changed their checking habits. The summary and TEAM attribution preserve that distinction.
The source attributes only the parser to the person and says coworkers changed their checking habits; it does not support personally achieving all the savings without help.
The source explicitly corrects the count to eight direct reports and says the person supervised those eight directly.
Five is explicitly corrected: the source says eight direct reports, not five.
The source explicitly identifies the 100-employee sentence as a misleading résumé example, not the person’s career history.
The source explicitly says the 100-employee sentence is not the person’s career history.
The source says the person received a SQL course-completion certificate and explicitly distinguishes it from a professional license.
The source explicitly says the person received a course-completion certificate, not a professional license.
The source says the person personally wrote SQL validation checks and that operators preferred a visible warning, with no implementation stated.
The source explicitly states that no implementation of the preferred warning was stated; it does not support that the person implemented it.
The source says the person personally implemented the visible warning and completed the rollout on 2024-06-30.
The source gives the rollout date as 2024-06-30, not 2024-05-31.
